reasoning: Corn ear showing dense white/cottony fungal mycelium covering kernels with some greenish areas. The thick white fluffy growth on kernels is characteristic of Diplodia ear rot (Stenocarpella maydis), which produces white cottony mycelium. Gibberella (pink), Aspergillus (olive-green), and Trichoderma (blue-green) do not match the predominantly white cottony appearance.
